newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Sunni militants burn Iranian centre in Lahore.
newsitem.headline: Sunni militants burn Iranian centre in Lahore.

text.p: Sunni Moslem militants mourning the death of their leader in a bomb blast attacked and burned an Iranian information centre in the Pakistani city of Lahore on Sunday, witnesses said.

They said activists of the Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) group set fire to the centre, located in a two-storey building in central Lahore, after thousands of people watched as the body of SSP leader Ziaur Rehman Faruqi was taken through the city.
Firemen were fighting the fire, which virtually gutted the information centre and spread to adjacent shops in the city's main Mall Road thoroughfare, the witnesses said.
People were evacuated from offices on the second floor of the building. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
Faruqi was among at least 19 people killed in a bomb blast at the Sessions Court in Lahore on Saturday, shortly before he and his deputy Azam Tariq were due to appear on murder charges.
Mourners earlier recited prayers for Faruqi at a mosque on Mall Road. He was due to be buried on Monday in his home town of Samundri, about 300 km (187 miles) south of Islamabad.
